mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%) compresses risk-free rates and increases the relative attractiveness of equities, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and the direction is positive due to the current rate level.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (as measured by 20-day rolling returns over the last 5 years).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 240 signals persistent inflation, prompting central bank tightening and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL is above 240 (as measured by 20-day rolling returns over the last 5 years).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is falling below 4.0%, it signals a tightening monetary policy cycle combined with a strong labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in 3 months AND UNRATE < 4.0%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in 3 months AND UNRATE < 4.0% (as measured by 20-day rolling returns over the last 5 years).

mechanism_narrative: In a high GDP growth regime (GDPC1 annualized growth rate > 2%), rising housing starts (HOUST > 1100) signal robust economic activity and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annualized growth rate > 2% AND HOUST > 1100
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 annualized growth rate > 2% AND HOUST > 1100 (as measured by 20-day rolling returns over the last 5 years).

mechanism_narrative: The industrial production index (INDPRO) above 100 signals strong economic activity and industrial output, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is always active and the direction is positive due to the current INDPRO level.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO is above 100 (as measured by 60-day rolling returns over the last 5 years).

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE reading above 5.0% signals a weak labor market and economic slowdown, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE is above 5.0% (as measured by 5-day rolling returns over the last 5 years).

mechanism_narrative: When the employment level (PAYEMS) is rising and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is falling below 4.5%, it signals a robust labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > 0.5% monthly AND UNRATE < 4.5%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS growth rate > 0.5% monthly AND UNRATE < 4.5% (as measured by 60-day rolling returns over the last 5 years).

mechanism_narrative: In a strong industrial production regime (INDPRO growth rate > 1% monthly), rising industrial output signals robust economic activity and supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO growth rate > 1% monthly (as measured by 5-day rolling returns over the last 5 years).
